title: Imperial Lates: Robots
desc:
At Imperial Lates: Robots, you can get hands-on with all things robots, tech and AI at this free evening event for adults. Where will robotics go in the next ten years, and what does intelligence mean in our ever changing world?

How would you feel about a robot doing surgery on you? Put your skills to the test by controlling a robotic arm to play our version of the classic game, Operation. title: FoNS Make-A-Difference! Competition Final
desc:
We are very pleased to invite you to the Faculty of Natural Sciences Make-a-Difference! Competition Final Judging Event which will take place on 28 October 2026 from 16.00.

The aim of the programme is to provide undergraduate students from across all Faculties with a forum to develop low-cost technology that would have a positive impact on society. The competition runs in 3 stages, with students working in teams to develop a low-cost technology idea. The top teams are given funding, lab space and a bursary to work on their project for 8 weeks over the summer.

At the final event, our teams will present their projects to a panel of VIP judges and an audience of staff, students and guests.

A drinks reception and buffet will follow the announcement of the winner.

title: Statistics Seminar: Massimo Franchi (Sapienza)
desc:
14:00 – 15:00 – Massimo Franchi

Title: Canonical correlation analysis of stochastic trends via functional approximation

Abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for semiparametric inference on the number s of common trends and their loading matrix ψ in I(1)/I(0) systems. It combines functional approximation of limits of random walks and canonical correlations analysis, performed between the p observed time series of length T and the first K discretized elements of an L2 basis. Tests and selection criteria on s, and estimators and tests on ψ are proposed; their properties are discussed as T and K diverge sequentially for fixed p and s. It is found that tests on s are asymptotically pivotal, selection criteria of s are consistent, estimators of ψ are T -consistent, mixed-Gaussian…

title: Junior Analysis Seminar – Monica Tapia del Moral (Cambridge)
desc:
Title

Abstract

The study of characteristic gluing was initiated by Aretakis, Czimek, and Rodnianski (2021), and has since proven to be an effective tool for constructing solutions to the Einstein equations. A remarkable example of this is the work of Kehle and Unger, who used it to construct solutions to the Einstein–Maxwell-charged scalar field system undergoing gravitational collapse to form an exactly extremal Reissner–Nordström black hole in finite time, disproving the so-called third law of black hole thermodynamics, and challenging the intuition that had prevailed for decades in much of the theoretical physics community. All these works focused on the Einstein equations with vanishing cosmological constant. In this talk, we discuss how these techniques can be extended to include…

title: Mathematical Physics Seminar (October 28th) – Ginestra Bianconi (QMUL) – Gravity from Entropy
desc:
Abstract: Gravity from Entropy (GfE) is a recently proposed theory deriving gravity from the GfE action coupling matter fields and spacetime geometry [1]. The fundamental idea is to associate the Lorentzian treat the spacetime metrics as quantum operators. The GfE Lagrangian is given by a novel Geometric Quantum Relative Entropy (GQRE) between the spacetime metric and the metric induced by matter fields and curvature. In doing so the GfE theory elevates the interplay between matter and geometry as the fundamental aspect of gravity to be reflected in its statistical mechanics and information theory action (the GfE action).

Location : Huxley 130, 15.00-16.00.
venue: Huxley 130, Huxley Building, South Kensington Campus

title: The good, the bad and the ugly of battery recycling
desc:
The good, the bad and the ugly of battery recycling

The Imperial Network of Excellence in Sustainability through Life Cycle Approaches will host Dr Jacqueline Edge and Dr Evangelos Kallitsis , who will deliver a talk on battery recycling in LCA.

Abstract:

As the battery industry scales up to meet Net Zero targets, a mountain of dead batteries looms, representing not only a waste of valuable resources, but also significant risks to human and environmental health. Battery materials, through production scrap and end-of-life batteries, are already being recovered through a range of methods, but there are concerns about the additional burdens that the current methods impose, through waste gases and contaminated water.
